title: Patterns Everywhere
about: Train a tiny model on labelled examples and watch it guess.

cards.prompt:
Teach a computer to tell **apples** from **bananas**. Label each fruit, then press Check.

The chart shows how round each fruit is (across) and how yellow (up). The computer will guess 3 new fruits by finding the example **closest** to each one.
cards.hint: Read each fruit's name: is it an apple or a banana?
cards.nudge: Check the names again. Every apple here is red and round, and every banana is long and yellow.
cards.explanation: Your labels were right. Then the computer guessed each new fruit's label from the **nearest** fruit you'd labelled. It got the red apple and the banana right, but called the **yellow apple** a banana. Why? See the next card.

cards.title: What just happened
cards.body:
You made **training data**: examples, each with a **label** saying what it is. From them the computer built a **model**, its own way of guessing labels for new things.

Every apple you showed it was red, so the yellow apple sat nearest the bananas. As far as the model knew, a yellow apple was just a very round banana.

cards.prompt: What would help this model most with yellow apples?

options.text: Add some yellow apples to its training data
Add lots more red apples, big and small
options.nudge: It already knows red apples well. What kind of apple is it missing?

options.text: Add more bananas, so it knows them better
options.nudge: The yellow apple got mixed up with bananas. Would more bananas teach it anything new about apples?

options.text: Remove the bananas from its training data
options.nudge: Then it couldn't recognise bananas at all. What could you add, instead of taking away?

cards.hint: The model only knows what it was shown. What was it never shown?
cards.explanation: The model went wrong because it had never seen a **yellow apple**. Adding some to its training data teaches it that apples can be yellow too. More red apples or more bananas teach it nothing new about apples, and removing the bananas would break the banana guesses.

cards.prompt: Here's the same [[model]], plus a **golden apple** it isn't using yet. Choose which examples to train on, so it gets **every** test fruit right.
cards.hint: Which example looks most like the yellow apple, but isn't being used yet?
cards.nudge: Leaving out the bananas makes it call everything an apple. What could you add instead?
cards.explanation: Adding the **golden apple** shows the model that apples can be yellow too. Now the yellow apple sits closest to an apple, and the bananas still help it recognise the ripe banana. Better examples, better guesses.

cards.prompt: You just taught a model about fruit. Put the steps of teaching a computer in order, from first to last.
cards.hint: Think about the fruit: you needed the fruit before you could label it, and you saw the model's guesses on new fruit before trusting it.
cards.nudge: Start with gathering the examples. What has to happen to them before the model can learn?
cards.explanation: First **collect** examples, then **label** them, then **train** the model on them. Before trusting it, **test** it on examples it hasn't seen, like your test fruit. Only then **use** it for real.

cards.prompt: Now there are three kinds of fruit. This [[model]] looks at the **3 nearest** examples and goes with the most common label. Label the fruit, then see its guesses.
cards.hint: The names tell you each fruit's label. Lemons are yellow and fairly round.
cards.nudge: Check the names again: each one says whether it's an apple, a banana or a lemon.
cards.explanation: Your labels were right. The model got the lemon and the red-and-yellow apple right, but its 3 nearest examples to the **yellow apple** were all lemons, so it guessed lemon. Again, it had never seen a yellow apple.

cards.prompt:
After you added the golden apple, the model got all 3 test fruits right. It only knows two labels: apple and banana.

Now someone shows it a **green pear**. Will it be right?

options.text: No: it can only answer apple or banana, so it must be wrong
Yes: it got every test right, so it's ready for any fruit
options.nudge: Passing 3 tests shows it's good at apples and bananas. What would it need to know to name a pear?

options.text: Yes: it will see the pear is new and make up a pear label
options.nudge: The model can only choose from the labels it was taught. Where would a new label come from?

options.text: Yes, if the pear sits closest to an apple on the chart
options.nudge: Then it would say apple. Is a pear an apple?

cards.hint: List every answer this model is able to give. Is "pear" one of them?
cards.explanation: The model can only pick from the labels it learned, so it will call the pear an **apple** or a **banana**, and be wrong either way. Passing its tests only shows it's good at the kinds of things it was tested on.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- **Training data** is examples, each with a **label** saying what it is.
- The computer finds patterns and builds a **model** to guess new things.
- It only knows what it was shown, so use varied examples.

Next: what AI can't do.
